summary: The article uses a September 2023 subway outage in Herald, caused by a failure in century-old track, to examine how aging infrastructure threatens public transit reliability. It covers the economic and social fallout, a UDRI study on infrastructure age, startup predictive-analytics solutions, proposed federal funding through the Forward Mobility Act, and 'Smarter City' visions for integrated mobility.
one_line: A September 2023 Herald subway outage illustrates how aging transit infrastructure causes costly disruptions, and the technology, funding and planning responses being proposed.
key_facts: On September 15, 2023, a failure in Herald's century-old track system caused an outage that halted the city's central line and stranded thousands of riders.
James McArthur, Head of the Herald Transit Authority (HTA), said the incident 'is symptomatic of a wider crisis' of transit systems relying on components 'designed for a bygone era'.
An Urban Development and Research Institute (UDRI) study released October 3, 2023 found approximately 70% of public transit infrastructure in major cities has been in use for over 50 years.
UDRI senior researcher Jennifer Alejo warned that without intervention, incidents like Herald's will become more commonplace.
The Herald outage reduced foot traffic for local businesses, forced students to reschedule exams, and disrupted parents' child care arrangements.
City University economics professor Greg Liang estimated the Herald incident cost the local economy $5 million in lost productivity and additional expenses.
On November 12, 2023, Boston-based startup TransitRevive announced a partnership with Herald to deploy predictive analytics and real-time monitoring across the subway network.
TransitRevive founder Emily Zhang said its AI-based systems let transit authorities move from reactive to proactive and optimize maintenance.
The Forward Mobility Act was introduced in the Senate on December 5, 2023, proposing a multifaceted funding approach to direct federal resources to public transportation.
Senator Elizabeth Marshall (D-NY) is a key proponent of the Forward Mobility Act and called it a leap toward sustainable, resilient public transportation.
Dr. Richard Tan heads the Smart Transit Hub project in San Francisco, which envisions autonomous shuttles, interconnected bike-share programs and energy-efficient light rail in a digitized framework.
